# Exact multivariate concave-radius truncation obstructions

The one-dimensional symmetric concave-sequence truncation theorem does not
extend by replacing its exponent with n+d. Nor does a proposed 2^(−n)
radial-contraction estimate hold in all dimensions. The counterexamples
below are restrictions of globally concave, even, unconditional radius
functions and arise as the actual fibers of full-dimensional convex bodies.
They do not disprove (OC).

## 1. A common actual-body realization

Fix integers n,d≥1 and 0<a<1. On [-1,1]^n define

    r(z)=1−(1−a)||z||_∞,
    T_d={x∈R^d:x_i≥0, Σ_i x_i≤1},
    C_(n,d,a)={(z,x):z∈[-1,1]^n, x∈r(z)T_d}.                 (1)

The radius is concave because the infinity norm is convex. It is even
and invariant under coordinate sign changes and permutations. In
particular its restriction to each coordinate line is concave.

The body in (1) is equivalently given by the finite linear inequalities

    −1≤z_j≤1,    x_i≥0,
    Σ_i x_i+(1−a)σ z_j≤1       for every j and σ∈{−1,1}.      (2)

It is therefore convex. It is compact because the displayed coordinates
are bounded, and it has interior: take z=0 and all x_i strictly positive
with sum less than a. Its integer projection is exactly {-1,0,1}^n.
Every actual fiber is r(z)T_d, and every one has positive d-volume.
At these integer bases,

    r(0)=1,    r(z)=a for all z≠0,
    Σ_z r(z)^d=1+(3^n−1)a^d.                                (3)

Thus the support is lattice-convex and centrally symmetric, and all the
strong radius hypotheses in the tested proposals hold.

## 2. The exponent n+d fails in the original truncation range

Take n=3,d=2,a=c=1/3. Since only the origin survives the truncation,

    Σ_z(r(z)−c)_+² = 4/9 = 972/2187,
    (1−c)^(n+d) Σ_z r(z)²
      = (2/3)^5(1+26/9) = 1120/2187.                         (4)

The proposed lower bound fails by exactly 148/2187. The threshold c=1/3
belongs to [1/3,1/2]. The failure therefore cannot be repaired merely by
restricting the threshold to the interval used in the chain problem.

A dimension-free exponent d+1 fails already for n=2,d=2,a=c=1/3:

    Σ_z(r(z)−c)_+² = 4/9 =108/243,
    (1−c)^(d+1)Σ_z r(z)² = (2/3)^3(1+8/9)=136/243.           (5)

The exact gap is 28/243. These sources satisfy coordinate concavity in
addition to global concavity, so those hypotheses do not rescue (5).

## 3. The proposed 2^(−n) centered contraction also fails

The separate proposed inequality was

    Σ_z(r(z)−c)_+^d
       ≥ 2^(−n)(1−c)^d Σ_z r(z)^d,       0≤c≤1/2.            (6)

Take n=4,d=2,a=c=1/2. Then

    Σ_z(r(z)−c)_+²=1/4=16/64,
    2^(−4)(1−c)²Σ_zr(z)²
      = (1/16)(1/4)(1+80/4)=21/64.                          (7)

Thus (6) fails by exactly 5/64. This example again has all the symmetries
and the actual-body realization proved in §1.

More generally, at a=c the only positive truncated radius is at zero.
Consequently (6) would require

    1+(3^n−1)c^d≤2^n.                                      (8)

For any fixed d and any fixed c>0, (8) fails for sufficiently large n.
The obstruction is therefore systematic rather than confined to one
small numerical configuration.

## 4. The peak-fiber centroid is not a universal mixed center

Use the actual body (1) with a=1/(d+1), and let

    y=(0,g),    g=(1/(d+1),...,1/(d+1))∈T_d.

This is the centroid of the largest, central fiber and is an actual
mixed-integer point. The ambient coordinate halfspace

    H={x_1≥1/(d+1)}                                         (9)

contains y. In every noncentral fiber aT_d its intersection has zero
d-volume (at most the single extreme vertex). In the central fiber its
volume is exactly γ_d|T_d|. Hence

    vol_MI(C∩Λ∩H)=γ_d|T_d|,
    vol_MI(C∩Λ)=|T_d|[1+(3^n−1)/(d+1)^d].                   (10)

Whenever

    1+(3^n−1)/(d+1)^d>2^n,                                 (11)

the point y fails the desired OC depth guarantee. For the concrete
choice n=6,d=2, the bracket in (10) is 737/9>64, so (11) holds exactly.
The cap has mass (4/9)|T_2|, whereas its required OC mass at that selected
point would be (4/9)|T_2|·737/576, strictly larger.

This refutes that particular peak-centroid selector. It is not an OC
counterexample: no upper bound on the depths of all other points is
asserted. In fact the reflected-fiber centerpoint construction in the
separate note `candidate c58c06a13eeebb18` gives a
mass-dependent point at the same integer base with a much larger valid
ambient depth for the n=6,d=2 example.
